directions.title: Cut / Carry
directions.plan: IDEA — A hard-edged editorial crop is the brand's visual signature: the opening portrait is not discarded at the hero boundary; its rust frame contracts and carries the same image into the first purchasable garment. PRIMARY JOURNEY — Monumental Marlow & Vale wordmark and campaign portrait → one controlled scroll transformation → filterable nine-garment catalogue with deliberately varied image scale → size selection and bag drawer → full size chart, care, shipping/returns and reviews → Leeds city/shop ending and the no-sales statement. The live route will preserve every exact product name, category, price, colour, fabric/detail sentence, sold-out size, measurement, care fact, regional shipping fact, review and shop fact from src/App.jsx; generated mockup microcopy is composition guidance only. SIGNATURE MOMENT — input: downward scroll; establish: portrait held in the rust crop; transform: page type clears while the frame shrinks and translates; hold: the frame locks around The Oxford Shirt at the top of the shop; handoff: filters, size controls and Add to bag become active around it; release: the frame becomes the recurring selected-item outline as the catalogue continues. MATERIAL — Generate a coherent set of representative fictional clothing imagery: one close editorial portrait, two supporting worn views, and nine clean garment views on warm neutral ground. These visuals will be explicitly treated as representative art direction, not verified inventory photography. Live typography/rules supply the print texture; no text is baked into production images. MOBILE — The portrait fills the first screen with the wordmark cropped at the edges; a short non-pinned transform lands it into a full-width first product, filters become a horizontally scrollable labelled rail, sizes stay 44px minimum, and the bag becomes a bottom sheet. REDUCED MOTION — Show the resolved shop composition immediately, use a simple opacity/crop swap rather than pinning or parallax, and keep every control available. IMPLEMENTATION — Semantic React shop state from the baseline; asymmetric CSS grid; GSAP ScrollTrigger/Flip for the single frame handoff and filter reflow; Lenis only for normal-motion desktop; CSS transitions for hover/focus and a focus-managed bag drawer. The lower route uses real HTML tables and accordions, not decorative screenshots. UNCERTAINTIES / RISK — The hero and first-product asset must share crop-compatible source material or the handoff will look like a dissolve; this needs an early production slice and motion capture. The mockup's generated small copy is not evidence of correctness. RELATIVE COST — Medium-high: one difficult transition plus a moderate coherent photo set, but the interaction model remains conventional after the handoff. RECOMMENDATION — Recommended overall because it creates the clearest perceptible continuity from editorial desire into buying while keeping the dense practical route visually calm.

directions.title: The Leeds Ledger
directions.plan: IDEA — The shop is a working cutting-table ledger: a mustard measuring tape begins inside the opening still life and becomes the continuous index that organizes filtering, products, sizing, proof and the final shop facts. PRIMARY JOURNEY — Overhead stack of garments and bold industrial wordmark → the measuring tape reaches punched category tabs → all nine garments laid out as a readable inventory with size controls and clipped order-docket bag → tape aligns the five-row size chart, care and three-region delivery information → reviews appear as pinned notes → the measure ends at 11 people / 1 Leeds shop / 4 named factories / never a sale. The live route will preserve every exact product name, category, price, colour, fabric/detail sentence, sold-out size, measurement, care fact, regional shipping fact, review and shop fact from src/App.jsx; generated labels and microcopy are spatial references only. SIGNATURE MOMENT — input: downward scroll; establish: physical tape beside the opening clothing stack; transform: tape unspools while the tabletop widens into the catalogue; hold: numbered marks align each product row and the active category tab; handoff: the same line becomes the size-chart axis; release: it passes through reviews and terminates beside the Leeds shop facts. MATERIAL — Generate nine consistent overhead folded/flat garment views, one workshop/model contact print, one workshop-wide closing image, and a small set of honest paper/cloth textures. Imagery is representative of fictional inventory, never claimed as verified product photography. The tape, rules, pins and order docket should be live CSS/SVG wherever possible rather than raster decoration. MOBILE — The tape becomes a slim left progress rail; products alternate image and information in one column; filter tabs are horizontally scrollable; the bag opens as a full-width docket sheet; dense tables scroll within clearly labelled regions. REDUCED MOTION — Keep the tape static at the left edge with active-section changes only; eliminate unspooling/parallax and reveal all content in normal document flow. IMPLEMENTATION — Semantic React catalogue and bag state; CSS grid and sticky section rail; a restrained ScrollTrigger path/position animation for the tape; CSS transforms for clipped notes and filter state; accessible native table and disclosure structures. UNCERTAINTIES / RISK — This direction depends on an unusually consistent overhead image set and disciplined texture density. If overworked it can become scrapbook theatre and reduce scanning speed, especially on mobile; texture must stay subordinate to labels and controls. The generated mockup includes illustrative microcopy that must not be trusted. RELATIVE COST — High: more asset production, responsive recomposition and decorative-layer QA than direction A, though its core motion is mechanically simpler. RECOMMENDATION — Strong alternative when tactile provenance and product comparison matter most, but not the overall recommendation: its continuous ledger is memorable yet risks visual busyness across the long factual tail.
